title: A structural call to a Unit method through a refinement whose result type is Any (or another supertype of Unit) returns null instead of ()
oracle: the same member called through a trait declaration with the same signature returns the boxed unit
generator: wave4/harness/fold/ctx.py, 'dyn' family (structural calls); found while choosing round-four structural contexts from CleanUp.transformApplyDynamic coverage, by a hand probe of the result-type branch of fixResult
seed: not recorded (hand probe written from coverage of CleanUp.fixResult)
detail: For class K { def m(x: Int): Unit } and (new K: { def m(x: Int): Any }).m(1), the call yields null. A Unit method conforms to a refinement member with result Any, so the call is well typed. CleanUp expands the call to Method.invoke, which returns null for a void method; fixResult boxes the result to BoxedUnit only when the refinement's own result type is Unit (resultSym == UnitClass) and passes it through unchanged when it is Object, although the code already computes isMaybeUnit for exactly this case and uses it only for arrays. The same member reached through a trait declaring def n: Any gets a bridge that returns BoxedUnit.UNIT. Ordinary code hits it when a structural type is written with a wide result type (Any, AnyVal, AnyRef is rejected) for a callback or close-like method; the result then compares unequal to () and throws NullPointerException on toString.
fix_sketch: When the refinement's erased result is Object, map a null result to BoxedUnit.UNIT if the resolved java.lang.reflect.Method's return type is void (Method.getReturnType == Void.TYPE), in the reflective call path. No binary compatibility cost; one extra check per reflective call with an Object result.
prior: none found; scala/bug#6199 is the same symptom in runtime reflection (fixed in 2.10); fork PRs 355, 394, 469, 437, 562 touch structural calls but not the result
